The correlative adjective *of what sort* is rendered by the whole frame *what manner of man*. Rule 91 makes the head the word the corpus already spends on this lexeme, and the corpus is unbroken: every interrogative or correlative adjective the ASV expands with *manner of* heads on *what* — 2PE.3.11 `ποταποὺς` → *what manner of persons*, the exact structural twin, and 1PE.1.11 `ποῖον`, JHN.12.33 and JHN.21.19 `ποίῳ`, JHN.18.32, 1JN.3.1 `ποταπήν` — six units on *what* and none on *manner*; `ὁποῖος` itself heads on the *what-* word at GAL.2.6, `ὁποῖοί` → *whatsoever*. *manner of man* is the frame and its generic completion, as *manner of persons* is at 2PE.3.11. Heading on *man* as the phrase's formal English noun is refused by rule 17, and heading on *manner* would rest on decomposing the Greek — that `ὁποῖος` adds a sortal element over a bare `τίς` — which is exactly the compositional argument rule 91 replaces with the query on the lemma. Rules 84 and 91 make an unbroken corpus a settled head, so this is not a rule 16 hedging case.

The supplied coordinating *and* joins two infinitives across an asyndetic Greek seam, and no source token licenses it (rule 5, with 2CO.3.7 and REV.15.6). The verse's two expressed `καί` tokens are both spent, on *and undefiled* and on *and widows*, and neither governs this juncture. Rule 88 is scoped to a participle converted into a coordinate finite clause and does not reach a seam between two infinitives both rendered as infinitives; rule 29's numeral juncture is narrower still. Rule 11 does not decide it either way — the ASV does italicize this *and* — and rule 37 is ruled out, no licensing conjunction standing in a neighbouring verse.

The Greek coordinates the two infinitives asyndetically — no καί stands between `ἐπισκέπτεσθαι` and `τηρεῖν`, the verse's two expressed conjunctions being spent on *and undefiled* and *and widows* — so the supplied *and* is `added` and only *to keep* stands here. Rule 88 does not reach it: that rule is scoped in terms to where the ASV **converts a Greek circumstantial participle into a coordinate finite clause**, and no conversion happens here, both infinitives being rendered as infinitives. 2CO.3.7 is the governing precedent and is the corpus's one test of that limit decided after rule 88 entered the contract: it marks the identical supplied *and* `added` across an asyndetic seam between two attributive participles, citing rule 5 with REV.15.6 and conceding nothing. Rule 86's test gives the same answer — a participle carries subordination, which is why rule 86 grants it a supplied *when* or *if*, but an infinitive carries no coordination, so no token licenses the juncture. TIT.2.9 `εἶναι` → *and to be* is the one contrary unit and is weak evidence: its note cites no rule and it was finished before rule 88 existed.
